newsitem.title: JAPAN: Naphtha prices fall in Tokyo, spreads wider.
newsitem.headline: Naphtha prices fall in Tokyo, spreads wider.

text.p: Toko naphtha prices were easier in quiet afternoon trade on Tuesday on the heels of weaker overnight crudes, while inter-month spreads remained firm amid healthy end-user demand, traders said.
Bids for first-half February open-spec naphtha were heard at $226.00 with no offers having surfaced.
"There's still very good demand from end-users," one trader said. "Sellers feel there's no need to rush to sell."
Second-half January was notionally assessed at $229.00/230.00, compared with $231.00/232.00 in late Monday trading.
The one-month spread from first-half January was bid at around plus $7.50 with no firm offers. It was discussed at plus $5.00/6.00 late last week.

Term naphtha talks between trading houses and petrochemical end-users for 1997 have yet to get into full swing, as the end-users are wary of a possible jump in premiums due to term price hikes by Middle Eastern producers, traders said.

The annual negotiations were usually close to an agreement at this time of year, they said. The delay in the talks prompted the end-users to seek more spot cargoes than usual for January delivery, they added. -- Tokyo Energy Desk
